answer.answer:
Take up objection c0001. It correctly identifies that semantic binding, active role, and contrast variation can be satisfied by a pre-existing rule component that P merely cites after the objection, so the objection can be counted as used even though it did not matter to the response. Rederiving from the challenged fork at step 12 with this objection present yields the same response-operative condition (1) already stated in the working position: D must be introduced or modified in P relative to P0, or P must record a decision to retain/select D because of C. No relation changes; the objection is already incorporated, and the kiln case is excluded.

Final Relation U: An objection O with content C is used for later request B and result R under published response P iff there exists a declared dependency set D of one or more components of P such that:
(1) D is semantically bound to C by a public mapping in P's text, change log, or rationale, and that mapping is response-operative: D is introduced or modified in P relative to P0, or P records a decision to retain/select D because of C rather than merely noting C. The binding is to C's represented condition, exception, priority, constraint, boundary clause, or public rejection of an alternative rule because it violates C, not to O's token identity or wording.
(2) D is active in the rule-application trace that derives R from B: the trace evaluates D and D affects the allocation role in R.
(3) Under the declared contrast for C, holding B and all rule components outside D fixed, the contrast rule state P^c (D replaced by the contrasting alternative, or the obstructed alternative restored) yields R^c, and R^c differs from R in a downstream allocation role. D may be a collective block; C need not be single-variable sufficient at the full endpoint.
(4) The R/R^c difference is not a dead branch and not a carrier detail.
(5) If the declared contrast or semantic mapping is missing, the checker cannot settle use from the specified evidence.

Specified evidence E: E1 timestamped objection transcript O; E2 pre-objection proposed rule P0; E3 published response P with change log, decision record, or rationale; E4 later booking request B, decision R, and rule-application trace with role bindings; E5 declared contrast set for C; E6 semantic mapping from C to D or to a rejected alternative, including whether D was introduced or retained because of C. The checker can test U by parsing C and E5, finding D and E6, checking trace E4, applying P and P^c to B, and comparing R and R^c for downstream role. The checker cannot settle: truth, validity, fairness, or wisdom of C; sincerity of the response author; hidden causes not in E; contested paraphrase if E6 is ambiguous; whether an unrecorded alternative would have been adopted absent O; or ethical quality of R.

Worked miniature: P0 says first-come-first-served for workshops. O says 'Do not allocate woodshop to a booking overlapping a safety-certification class.' C is that conditional constraint. P1 says 'For woodshop requests, if the time overlaps a safety-certification class, assign makerspace; otherwise assign the requested workshop,' and the change log cites O and records adoption of the exception because of C. D is the exception component. B is Alice requesting woodshop Tuesday 10-12 with a safety class Tuesday 10-11. The trace applies D and R is makerspace. The contrast removes D or negates C; P^c assigns woodshop to Alice. R^c differs in the downstream allocation role. So O was used.

Dead branch: Same O, but P1 only stores a comment 'objection noted: no woodshop during safety class' while the rule remains first-come-first-served; B gets woodshop. Or P1 has D but its output is cancelled or overwritten by a later default with no trace and no downstream role. The contrast leaves R unchanged. That is stored beside, not used.

Counterexample that would show a weaker proposed narrowing wrong: Suppose O says 'Never double-book the kiln.' P0 already contains K1 = no overlapping kiln bookings. P1 merely adds a change-log line 'objection noted' and cites O, but there is no decision record that K1 was introduced or retained because of C. For B, K1 is active and the contrast removes K1, so R changes from denied to allowed. A relation U that only requires semantic binding, active role, and contrast would count O as used. But the objection did not matter to the decision process; the rule already did the work and the citation is post hoc. This counterexample requires condition (1) to include the response-operative clause above: D must be introduced/modified in P or a decision record must show D was retained/selected because of C. It preserves the later task because a merely stored objection still fails the response-operative test, while a used objection must still show a downstream allocation difference under contrast.

If an even stronger counterexample were produced—one where D is response-operative, active, and contrast-changing, yet independent evidence shows the decision was made before O arrived—then condition (1) would need a temporal/causal ordering check using E1 and E3 timestamps. That would not collapse the narrowing; it would add an evidential ordering requirement and preserve the same downstream-role test.

claims.quote: Final Relation U: An objection O with content C is used for later request B and result R under published response P iff there exists a declared dependency set D of one or more components of P such that:
claims.value: Final relation U requires response-operative semantic binding, active role in the trace, contrast variation that changes downstream allocation role, exclusion of dead branches and carrier details, allows collective blocks, and leaves use unsettled if contrast or mapping is missing. The open objection c0001 is taken up and its response-operative correction is already incorporated; no relation changed.

derivation_steps.statement: Extract from the quoted FW5 passage the active-route requirements: actual occurrences, a connected input-to-result route, component relations and role bindings, nonconstant dependence under declared contrasts, exclusion of dead branches and carrier details, and allowance of collective blocks. Commitment: the narrowing must respect these requirements. Falsified if the passage is read to require single-variable necessity at the full endpoint or to ignore role bindings.

Identify the later-task entities: objection O with content C, published response P, later booking request B, and downstream result R. Commitment: these entities are the relevant public relata. Falsified if the later task lacks any of them or if the objection is only stored without a P or R.

Specify the evidence E1-E6 needed to check a relation: objection transcript, pre-objection rule, published response and rationale or decision record, booking decision trace, declared contrasts, and semantic mapping. Commitment: the checker uses E1-E6, and missing contrast or mapping blocks settling use. Falsified if a checker could settle use from less evidence or if these evidence are unavailable.

Define semantic binding: C must map publicly to a dependency set D in P or to a rejected alternative because it violates C, not to token ID or wording. Commitment: binding is to C's represented condition, exception, priority, constraint, boundary clause, or rejected alternative. Falsified if D is bound only by co-occurrence, token identity, or wording.

Define active role: D must be evaluated in the trace that derives R from B and affect the allocation role in R. Commitment: inert, cancelled, or overwritten components do not satisfy active role. Falsified if an inert or overwritten D is treated as active.

Define contrast: holding B and other components fixed, varying D or the public alternative must change R to R^c in a downstream allocation role; D may be a collective block and C need not be single-variable sufficient at the full endpoint. Commitment: the contrast tests dependence on D, not mere presence. Falsified if variation of D leaves the downstream allocation unchanged or changes only a carrier detail.

Exclude dead branches and carrier details: cancelled or overwritten outputs without downstream role and mere wording, format, channel, identifier, or timing changes do not count. Commitment: such items cannot supply the dependence. Falsified if such an item changes the downstream allocation under the declared contrast.

State relation U as the conjunction of semantic binding, active role, contrast variation, and exclusions; its negation is stored beside. Commitment: O is used iff some D satisfies these conditions. Falsified if a case satisfies all conditions but is merely stored, or fails one condition yet is used.

State the checker procedure: parse C and contrasts, find D and mapping, inspect trace, apply P and P^c to B, compare downstream R and R^c; where mapping or alternative is missing, use is not settled. Commitment: the procedure is the public test. Falsified if the procedure accepts a stored objection or rejects a used one under E1-E6.

Give the worked miniature of the woodshop safety objection and show the contrast changes Alice's allocation from makerspace to woodshop. Commitment: the exception component is semantically bound, active, and contrast-changing. Falsified if P^c yields the same allocation or if the change is not in a downstream allocation role.

Give the dead-branch case: the objection is stored in a comment or an overwritten condition and the contrast leaves the downstream allocation unchanged. Commitment: this is stored beside, not used. Falsified if a stored objection nevertheless changes R through a traceable D.

With objection c0001 present, the pre-existing kiln rule K1 case shows that a relation requiring only semantic binding, active role, and contrast would count O as used although K1 already did the work and P merely cites O post hoc. Commitment: the weaker relation is wrong. Falsified if the case actually contains a decision record introducing or retaining K1 because of C.

Revise U by adding the response-operative condition: D must be introduced or modified in P relative to P0, or P must record a decision to retain/select D because of C. Commitment: a merely stored objection fails, while a used objection still needs a downstream allocation difference under contrast; if needed, add a temporal/causal ordering check using E1 and E3. Falsified if a merely stored objection passes the response-operative test or if a used objection lacks it but is nevertheless used.

objections.target_claim: The AFTER ANSWER revision (the added response-operative clause) is necessary: without it, a pre-existing rule component cited post hoc by P would satisfy the relation and the objection would be counted as used.
objections.text: Check-bearing objection to the unrevised BEFORE ANSWER relation. The genuine answer step under R3-A2 is the recognition that an objection can be semantically bound, active, and contrast-changing yet not have mattered to the response, because the rule already did the work. The public case is: P0 already contains the kiln no-overlap rule K1; O says 'Never double-book the kiln'; P1 merely adds 'objection noted' and cites O; for B, K1 is active and contrast variation of K1 changes R. The BEFORE ANSWER relation counts O as used, but the objection did not matter to the decision process. This defeats the unrevised condition (1) rather than the final response-operative version.
